data.why: The repo bundles the processed NASA Exoplanet Archive catalog (data/processed/exoplanets_clean.csv) and the dashboard model assets (data/dashboard/*) that app.py reads directly, so no files need to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Characterize how the observed exoplanet population differs by discovery method (Transit, Radial Velocity, Microlensing) across radius, mass, period, and temperature
Filter confirmed planets by discovery year range and discovery method to explore subpopulation trends over time
Inspect the mass-radius and period-temperature relationships on log-log scales to identify correlations and selection effects
Review statistical comparisons (Transit vs Radial Velocity) with effect sizes to judge whether differences are large and robust
Evaluate the Random Forest mass-prediction model's held-out performance, feature importances, and error broken down by discovery method
Look up an individual confirmed planet's physical parameters and, if held out during testing, its predicted vs cataloged mass

review.summary: The tree covers both of the README's aims (how discovery method shapes the observed population, and held-out evaluation of the mass model), follows the six dashboard stages at a sensible depth, and every screen I checked matches what its node says. It needs small wording fixes before filing: the period–temperature plot is called 'log-log' when its temperature axis is linear, one inference is stated as fact, and a few actions sit under the wrong task.
